title: William Stephenson's Caribbean activities and ties to scientists

tellings.quote: And he was doing a lot of stuff in and around the Caribbean, the Bahamas, the Virgin Islands.

plain: In the 1940s, the wartime intelligence figure William Stephenson was, Michels says, doing "a lot of stuff" around the Caribbean, the Bahamas and the Virgin Islands, and had ties to scientists such as the electrical engineer Charles Steinmetz and the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, linking Stephenson also to the American spy chief Bill Donovan and the publisher Robert Maxwell. If true, it would tie secret wartime intelligence work to fringe science and to later powerful networks.
